prompt:
Create a photoreal photographic atlas with overall 16:9 canvas, ideally 2560x1440. Exactly TWO columns by THREE rows: six independent 8:3 panoramic photos with NO gutters/borders. The attached reference contains each scene in matching tile order. Each photo is an overhead view of real cream cardstock evidence cards on a laboratory tabletop. Left column warm wood, right column gray stone, distinct believable photographs. Keep ALL card text in upper 75% of each tile; bottom25% plain tabletop. No other cards, science examples or specimens, no electron configurations anywhere.
Every tile contains a prominent left element card and a wider printed worksheet card to right, realistic paper texture and lighting. Right card header "GROUND-STATE CONFIGURATION", a big gold question mark "?" inside a large otherwise EMPTY box, small text "choose an answer in the workspace". Beneath cards a note with the relevant element name and "answer hidden until submitted".
TOP ROW left element card "Mg" and "Z = 12"; note "Magnesium · answer hidden until submitted".
MIDDLE ROW left element card "Cr" and "Z = 24"; note "Chromium · answer hidden until submitted".
BOTTOM ROW left element card "Cu" and "Z = 29"; note "Copper · answer hidden until submitted".
All six photos reproduce the question state of their reference. Do not fill the empty box with a solution, orbital diagram or sample configuration. Do not add a footer caption. No handwriting, people, logos or watermark. Ensure each tile is one coherent photographed scene and contains none of the neighboring tile.
review: All six cards visually checked: Mg Z=12, Cr Z=24, Cu Z=29; ground-state configuration remains a question mark with no revealed answer. Correct element names and workspace instruction. No neighboring scene leaks. Actual seams inspected.
